title: Spin pumping reveals vortex-mediated angular-momentum dissipation at the superconducting transition
authors: Maximilian Mangold, Alex Burg, Franz Weidenhiller, Thomas N. G. Meier, Hiroto Adachi, Lin Chen, Christian Back
abstract: Spin pumping into superconductors is generally expected to become less efficient below the critical temperature $T_\textrm{c}$ because quasiparticle transport freezes out. Here we report a pronounced enhancement of the spin pumping-induced magnetic damping in Py/Nb heterostructures, confined to a narrow temperature interval immediately below the superconducting transition. The damping exceeds its normal-state value and therefore cannot be explained within the conventional quasiparticle picture of spin transport. The enhancement coincides with the finite-resistance vortex-creep regime of the Nb layers and disappears upon cooling into the pinned vortex state, indicating that mobile Abrikosov vortices provide an additional channel for spin-angular-momentum dissipation. These results establish ferromagnetic resonance as a sensitive probe of dissipative vortex dynamics in superconductors.
summary: This research reports an enhancement of spin pumping-induced magnetic damping in superconducting heterostructures that occurs only in a narrow temperature window below $T_c$. This enhancement is found to perfectly coincide with the regime of mobile Abrikosov vortices undergoing creep. The findings establish that these mobile vortices act as a novel, significant channel for dissipating angular momentum in superconductors.
main_problem: To determine if mobile Abrikosov vortices provide an additional channel for spin-angular-momentum dissipation beyond conventional quasiparticle transport in superconductors near the critical temperature.
main_result: The enhanced magnetic damping observed immediately below $T_c$ correlates precisely with the resistive vortex-creep regime, strongly indicating that mobile vortices mediate this additional dissipation channel.
method: The study combines broadband Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) measurements to probe damping ($\alpha_{eff}$) with electrical transport measurements ($R(T)$) to map the vortex-creep regime.
model_or_system: The system involves Py/Nb heterostructures where the superconductor (Nb) hosts Abrikosov vortices. The physics is analyzed by comparing the temperature dependence of the damping enhancement to the known resistive vortex-creep dynamics.
key_observables: Effective Gilbert damping parameter ($\alpha_{eff}$), magnetic anisotropy field ($\Delta H_{an}$), and electrical resistance ($R/R_n$).
important_parameters: Critical temperature ($T_c$), vortex-creep regime temperature window ($\sim 0.1 T_c$), and superconducting coherence length ($\xi$).
main_assumptions: The enhancement is attributed to mobile vortices, as other known superconducting mechanisms predict different, broader temperature dependencies.
figures_summary: Figures show the overlap between the temperature dependence of excess damping and the resistive vortex-creep tail, confirming the correlation between the two phenomena.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by noting the expected quasiparticle freeze-out below $T_c$, then presents FMR/transport data showing an anomalous damping enhancement coinciding with vortex-creep, and finally argues that this correlation proves the vortex-mediated dissipation mechanism.
why_interesting: The work provides a direct, measurable link between macroscopic transport phenomena (vortex motion) and fundamental quantum properties (spin dissipation) in superconductors, offering a new diagnostic tool for vortex dynamics.
